legend: The Brown Lady of Raynham Hall (Norfolk, England, 1936 photograph)
lines: Norfolk, England, 1936. A grand old house, and a very old legend.
They say a woman in a brown dress walks the halls of Raynham Hall.
Legend says she was Lady Dorothy Walpole, locked inside by her husband in the early 1700s.
Guests swore she glided down the staircase, with empty, glowing eyes.
Even a famous sea captain, Frederick Marryat, claimed he met her.
Then, in 1936, two photographers set up a camera facing that very staircase.
One of them whispers: quick, there is something on the stairs. He takes the shot.
The photo shows a pale, see-through figure drifting down the steps.
Experts call it a double exposure or a trick of the light.
But nobody has proved it. What do you see?
title: The Ghost Photo That Experts Still Can't Explain... 👻📸 #shorts
description:
In 1936, two photographers shot a staircase at Raynham Hall in England and the picture seemed to show a ghostly woman. Legend says she is the Brown Lady. Real ghost or a trick? This is the legend of the Brown Lady of Raynham Hall.
